name: Maligo
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.note: No stress statement; identifies '(N1) Maligo (ǃxuun, kúándò ǃxuun "Kwando ǃXuun"; SE Angola)' following Heine & König's dialect labels; only 'It also has tone and nasalization.'

sources.citation: Miller, Amanda & Micha Elsner. 2017. Click reduction in fluent speech: a semi-automated analysis of Mangetti Dune !Xung. Proc. 2nd Workshop on Computational Methods in the Study of Endangered Languages (ACL W17-0115), 107-115.
sources.note: Nothing on word stress; phonetic click study of Mangetti Dune !Xung (ex-[gfx], also merged into [vaj]); notes stimuli 'vary in terms of tone and phonation type' and 'weaker prosodic positions' (phrasal), no stress statement.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2014. Change Request Number 2014-057 (merge [gfx] Mangetti Dune !Xung, [mwj] Maligo, [oun] !O!ung into [vaj] Vasekele). SIL International.
sources.note: Nothing; identity only: Maligo is 'only an alternate name for Vasekele' (Northern !Kung); cites Sands 2010 and Kirk Miller p.c.

sources.citation: Heine, Bernd & Henry Honken. 2010. The Kx'a family: a new Khoisan genealogy. Journal of Asian and African Studies (Tokyo) 79: 5-36.
sources.note: Comparative. Table 1 identifies dialect N1 '!xuun or kúándò !xuun (Kwando !Xun), Southeastern Angola' (= Maligo). Sec. 2.5: 'most !Xun dialects distinguish four tone levels and four register tonemes in addition to contour tones'; nothing on stress. Notes grammatical data exist only for E1, E2, W1, W2.

sources.citation: Grimes, B. (ed.) 2000. Ethnologue 14th ed., entry MALIGO [MWJ]; Lewis, M.P. (ed.) 2009. Ethnologue 16th ed., entry Maligo [mwj] (Wayback copies).
sources.note: Nothing; entries give only Angola, 'Khoisan, Southern Africa, Northern', pop. 2,230 (2000); no location, no linguistic data.

sources.citation: Bleek, Dorothea F. 1928. Bushmen of Central Angola. Bantu Studies 3: 105-125 (archive.org african-studies_1927-1929_3, scanned text).
sources.note: Nothing. First-hand 1925 visit to !kun on the Kutsi (Kwando tributary) and Kunzumbia/Lomba rivers, i.e. the N1/Kwando !Xun area; LANGUAGE section (p.125) only notes youths dropping initial clicks and Nyemba loans; no tone or stress remarks.
